conceptBreakdown.heading: 1.1 IUPAC Name Architecture
conceptBreakdown.title: 1.1 IUPAC Name Architecture

summaryBox.title: IUPAC Framework
summaryBox.takeaway: Secondary Prefix (Substituents) → Primary Prefix (Cyclo/Bicyclo) → Root Word (C-Chain length) → Primary Suffix (Alkane/ene/yne) → Secondary Suffix (Principal Functional Group).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
IUPAC NAME ARCHITECTURE
                                    │
   [ Secondary Prefix ] ──► [ Primary Prefix ] ──► [ Root Word ] ──► [ Primary Suffix ] ──► [ Secondary Suffix ]
   (Substituents/Cl,Me)    (Cyclo/Bicyclo)       (C-Chain length)  (Alkane/ene/yne)      (Principal Functional)
conceptBreakdown.content:
Organic compounds are systematically named according to IUPAC rules:

1. **Root Word**: Indicates the length of the longest continuous principal carbon chain (*meth-, eth-, prop-, but-, pent-, hex-, etc.*).
2. **Primary Suffix**: Indicates saturation/unsaturation (*-ane, -ene, -yne*).
3. **Secondary Suffix**: Identifies the principal functional group (*-oic acid, -al, -one, -ol, -amine*).
4. **Primary Prefix**: Distinguishes cyclic/acyclic framework (*cyclo-, bicyclo-, spiro-*).
5. **Secondary Prefix**: Denotes substituents/side chains (*chloro-, bromo-, methyl-, nitro-, alkoxy-*).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 1.2 Principal Functional Group Priority Hierarchy
conceptBreakdown.title: 1.2 Principal Functional Group Priority Hierarchy
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
FUNCTIONAL GROUP PRIORITY ORDER (HIGHEST TO LOWEST)

   -COOH > -SO₃H > -COOR > -COX > -CONH₂ > -CN > -CHO > -C=O > -OH > -SH > -NH₂ > -C=C- > -C≡C-
conceptBreakdown.content:
When a molecule contains multiple functional groups, the highest-ranking group serves as the **Principal Functional Group** (Secondary Suffix), while all lower priority groups are named as **Secondary Prefixes (Substituents)**:

• $-\text{COOH}$ (*-oic acid* / *Carboxy-*)
• $-\text{SO}_3\text{H}$ (*-sulfonic acid* / *Sulfo-*)
• $-\text{COOR}$ (*-oate* / *Alkoxycarbonyl-*)
• $-\text{COX}$ (*-oyl halide* / *Halocarbonyl-*)
• $-\text{CONH}_2$ (*-amide* / *Carbamoyl-*)
• $-\text{CN}$ (*-nitrile* / *Cyano-*)
• $-\text{CHO}$ (*-al* / *Formyl-* or *Oxo-*)
• $-\text{COR}$ (*-one* / *Oxo-* or *Keto-*)
• $-\text{OH}$ (*-ol* / *Hydroxy-*)
• $-\text{SH}$ (*-thiol* / *Mercapto-*)
• $-\text{NH}_2$ (*-amine* / *Amino-*)
• $-\text{C=C}-$ (*-ene*) $>$ $-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-$ (*-yne*).

quickRevision: -COOH has the highest priority among all functional groups.
Double bonds take priority over triple bonds when deciding numbering direction in a tie.
All functional groups lower than the principal group are named as prefixes in alphabetical order.
